## Overview

The Sur are described as a historical Pashtun tribe from among the Lodi, living primarily in what is now Afghanistan and Pakistan. The founder of the Sur Empire in India, Sher Shah Sur, belonged to the tribe. The Sur ruled the Sur Empire from 1540 until they were removed from power in 1555 after the Battle of Sirhind by Humayun and the Persian army, which re-established the Mughal Empire. The sources also describe a separate Sur–Myet language of Bauchi and Plateau states in Nigeria, known by the names *kuSur*, *Nsur*, *Tapshin*, and *Myet*. The relationship between this language community and the historical Pashtun tribe is not explained by the sources.

## Material culture

### Architecture

The Suri tribe of the Afghans is described as having inhabited the mountains of Ghor east of Furrah. Its principal cities were Ghore, Feruzi, and Bamian.

## Oral tradition & literature

The sources mention a mythical-origin account in which some descriptions trace the Sur’s descent from the Arab general Khalid ibn al-Walid. They also identify Sher Shah Sur as the founder of the Sur Empire in India.

## Language & religion

Sur–Myet, also known as *kuSur*, *Nsur*, *Tapshin*, or *Myet*, is described as a minor Plateau language of Bauchi and Plateau states in Nigeria. It has two closely related dialects, Súr and Myet, and about 16,000 speakers. Sur speakers are surrounded by Ngas speakers, who refer to the Sur as Dishili. The language is described as still being passed on to children and not immediately endangered.
